Fit the marginal mixed-model lens

Source: R/lens_glmm_marginal.R
fit_glmm_marginal.Rd

Runs the koine-authored No-U-Turn Sampler on the random-effects marginal model — the random intercepts integrated out, exactly for the Gaussian LMM and by adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature for a GLMM — and returns an fb_fit() of (beta, sigma, tau) draws. For the Poisson marginal — whose variance-component funnel a single static-metric kernel cannot traverse — a funnel-safe blocked sampler is used: log tau is slice-sampled, and the coefficients are slice-sampled along their tau-resolved principal axes (a Gibbs block that needs no step size and cannot stall); the Gaussian and binomial marginals keep the joint NUTS kernel.

Usage

fit_glmm_marginal(
  pass,
  lens_spec = NULL,
  n_iter = 1500L,
  n_burn = 750L,
  n_chains = 4L,
  n_nodes = 20L,
  max_treedepth = 9L
)

Arguments

pass

A koine_pass carrying a single random intercept (1 | g), or the MET structure of two crossed/nested random intercepts (1 | variety) + (1 | trial).

lens_spec

The lens's registry record; defaults to the registry's glmm_marginal record.

n_iter

Iterations per chain (including warm-up). The Hamiltonian kernel needs far fewer than a random walk for the same effective sample size, so the default is modest.

n_burn

Warm-up iterations per chain (step-size + mass-matrix adaptation), discarded from the returned draws.

n_chains

Number of chains.

n_nodes

Gauss-Hermite nodes for the GLMM marginal (ignored for the exact Gaussian LMM path).

max_treedepth

Maximum NUTS tree depth (the joint-NUTS Gaussian / binomial path only), capping the leapfrog budget per iteration at 2^max_treedepth; saturation of the cap is surfaced in the provenance trace, never silently absorbed. The Poisson blocked slice kernel has no tree depth.

Value

A koine_fb_fit, or a koine_abstention for an unsupported pass.

Details

For the breeder-standard multi-environment-trial (MET) structure — two crossed or nested random intercepts (1 | variety) + (1 | trial) — the Gaussian marginal stays exact (a dense Cholesky of V = sigma^2 I + sum_r tau_r^2 Z_r Z_r') and is sampled by a coordinate-wise slice kernel over (beta, sigma, tau_variety, tau_trial); the draws then carry one tau_<grouping> per random factor. A non-Gaussian MET (a dense crossed-GLMM marginal, which has no exact quadrature) returns a lens-scope abstention(). The pointwise log-likelihood is left NULL for assemble_loglik() to compute as the per-observation integrated predictive (F3). If the pass carries no supported random intercept, returns a lens-scope abstention() rather than a wrong fit (I1).

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
g <- factor(rep(1:8, each = 5))
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(40), g = g)
d$y <- 1 + 0.5 * d$x + rnorm(8)[g] + rnorm(40, 0, 0.7)
pass <- koine_pass(y ~ x + (1 | g), d, gaussian())
fit_glmm_marginal(pass, n_iter = 800L, n_burn = 400L, n_chains = 2L)
# }
